parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `PlaybackController` live in the same `Playback` package and share a handful of surface-level method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `play`, `stop`), the structural evidence confirms zero shared fields (`shared_field_count: 0`) and a null Jaccard similarity. The two protocols operate at distinct abstraction layers: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` is a low-level AVAudioEngine wrapper (exposing `eventStream:AsyncStream<AudioPlayerEvent>`, `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `volume`, `makeRenderTapStream`) while `PlaybackController` is a higher-level domain controller (exposing `state:PlaybackState`, `isLoading`, `toggle:(reason: PlaybackReason)`, `makeAudioBufferStream`). Forcing a parent–child inheritance relationship would couple unrelated concerns and leak engine-level details into the domain protocol boundary. The overlapping names (`play`, `stop`, `installRenderTap`) have different signatures across the two protocols (e.g., `play:() throws` vs `play:(reason: PlaybackReason) throws`), making a shared parent impractical without signature changes.
